page.layout: One page of text in a single column; below the text three footnotes in smaller type, marked with superscript letters f, g, h. Running head at top centre, page number at top left.

main_text.p: and poetry, and be continually delighted with such as did more accurately set forth her praises:" (even as Homer bringeth in Apollo, tickledf at the heart with hearing the songs that were made unto him in the camp of the Grecians :) of which he produceth two special instances, the one of Alypius the grammarian, unto whom being forsaken of the physicians, Thecla (he saith) did appear in the night, and demanded of him, what he ailed, and what he would. He to shew his art, and to win the virgin's favour with the aptness of the verse, returneth for an answer unto her that verse, wherewith Homer maketh Achilles to answer his mother Thetis, in the first of the Iliads:
main_text.l: Οἶσθα· τίη ταῦτ' εἰδυίη πάντ' ἀγορεύω;
Thou knowest; why should I tell thee that knowest all?
main_text.p: Whereat "theg martyr smiling, and being delighted partly with the man, partly with the verse, and wondering that he had answered so aptly," conveyed a certain round stone unto him, with the touch whereof he was presently set on foot from his long and perilous sickness. For the other instance, the writer reporteth that which happened unto himself: for "theh martyr," saith he, "is such a lover of learning, and taketh such a delight in these oratorious praises, that I will tell somewhat of those things that were done to myself and for myself: which the martyr, who did it, doth know to have been done, and that I lie not." Then he telleth, how having prepared an oration for her anniversary festivity, the day before it should be pronounced, he was taken with such an extreme pain
f Μελπόντες ἑκαίργον· ὁ δέ, φρένα τέρπετ' ἀκούων. Homer. Iliad. α.
g Ἐπιμειδιάσασα γοῦν ἡ μάρτυς, καὶ ἡσθεῖσα ἐπί τε τῷ ἀνδρί, ἐπί τε τῷ ἔπει, θαυμάσασα δὲ καὶ ὡς μάλα ἁρμοδίως ἀπεκρίνατο. Basil. Seleuc. de miraculis S. Theclæ, lib. 2. cap. 24.

h Οὕτω δὲ φιλόλογός ἐστιν ἡ μάρτυς, καὶ χαίρει ταῖς ὑπὸ τῶν λόγων ταύταις εὐφημίαις. ἐρῶ τι καὶ τῶν ἐμαυτῷ καὶ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ γεγονότων, ὑπερ αὐτὴ ἡ παρασχηκυῖα μοι μάρτυς οἶδεν ὅτι γεγένηται, καὶ οὐ ψεύδομαι. Ibid. cap. 27.

page.notes: Footnote marks in the text are superscript letters f, g, h, written here as sup tags. The verse line in Greek and the English gloss below it are printed in italic and roman respectively. Possible misprint: "tickled" appears as printed. Footnote f reads "Iliad. α." as printed.
